lead: Tampa plumbing deals with heat, storms, storm surge and old cast-iron drains. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Tampa.
risk: cast-iron drain failures, slab leaks and storm and surge flooding
risk_short: cast-iron drains, slab leaks and flooding
why: Seminole Heights, Hyde Park and Tampa Heights have homes from the early 1900s, and many mid-century homes have cast-iron drains under the slab that are rotting from the inside.
Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024 showed how surge and rain can flood low areas and back up sewers. Homes built from the late 1970s to the mid-1990s may have polybutylene pipe.
water: Tampa's water comes mainly from the Hillsborough River, with backup supply from Tampa Bay Water. It is moderately hard, so scale slowly builds up in water heaters and on fixtures.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Have the water heater checked after a flood.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in South Tampa, Hyde Park, Davis Islands, Seminole Heights, Westchase, New Tampa and every other Tampa neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Tampa Construction Services Center, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: What plumbing checks should Tampa homes get after a hurricane?
faq.a: Have a plumber check the water heater, gas lines and the sewer line, especially if water got into the home. Silt and debris can clog drains, and surge water damages heater controls.
